params.body:
A card holding three lines of text was two hundred pixels tall. That looked like a design choice and it was a name collision.

## The cause

`public/template/css/style.min.css`, the bought theme, carries Bootstrap's spacing utilities **with `!important`**:

```css
.py-5 { padding-top: 3rem !important; padding-bottom: 3rem !important }
.px-5 { padding-right: 3rem !important; padding-left: 3rem !important }
```

Tailwind uses the same names for other values — `py-5` is 1.25 rem there — and cannot outrank `!important` whatever order the stylesheets load in. So every `px-5 py-5` on the Activiteit screen asked for twenty pixels of padding and was handed forty-eight. The same holds for `p-1`, `py-3` and `py-4`, which is precisely the set this screen used to set its rhythm.

Nothing broke, nothing errored, and the page had looked "a bit airy" since the day it was built.

## The fix

The screen's measurements are its own `.act-` classes in `resources/css/insights.css` instead of Tailwind utilities. Not a preference: while Bootstrap and Tailwind stand side by side, a spacing class here is a guess.

Cards are 14 by 18 rather than 48 all round, rows are 3 pixels apart instead of 4, and the whole panel is 880 pixels wide rather than Tailwind's `max-w-4xl` (896) — close enough that it was never the width that made it feel empty.

## Two smaller things in the same screen

**Hover was missing.** The measure and period options had no hover state at all, so nothing said they could be clicked. They now take ink and a grey underline on hover and on keyboard focus.

**The tabs changed weight when you switched.** The active tab was `font-weight: 600` against 400; Poppins ships those as separate faces, so the text visibly re-set itself and read as a different typeface. Both tabs are 500 now, and the active one is marked by colour and the groove under it. That is also what the house guide asks: colour lives in the moving part, and a meter is a groove.

## Verified

`TheThemeOverrulesEverySpacingClassTest` reads the theme for every class it declares `!important` and requires the Activiteit markup to use none of them. It is derived from the theme rather than a hardcoded list, so it catches the next collision too, not only padding.

Checked by mutation: putting `py-5` back on the root fails it by name.

Only that screen is held to this. The other tab **is** the theme's own Bootstrap markup and uses those classes on purpose; forbidding them there would be forbidding the theme.

New rule R P3-16.12. `npm run build` green, `phpstan` green, `pint` green on the added file. Local suite: the same nine failures as on a clean `main` in my environment; CI runs on a fresh database.

## Still open

The screen needs more than spacing. Drill-down from a number to the rows behind it is still missing, and the two tabs still wear different clothes — the Zaak tab is Bootstrap, this one is not. Both are their own change.
params.title: The theme overrules every spacing class
